new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (3 pp., SIL-PNG Organised Phonology Data, 'Nekgini (Nekeni) Language [NKG], Rai Coast - Madang Province', data checked by P. Lillie; PDF created 2004). extracted text of page 2 shows, under the heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', exactly: 'Stress does not seem to be phonemic. / Tone is not found. / All the vowels have lengthened counterparts, but context determines whether the vowel is long or short so length does not need to be.' -- verbatim as quoted, locator p.2 correct. I read the whole sheet: consonant/vowel inventories with example words (no stress marks anywhere), two notes on dialect variation (r/l, g/k; ng+g), the suprasegmentals lines, syllable patterns (V, CV,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only first-hand statement says stress is (tentatively) non-contrastive and the language is not tonal; it does not say on which syllable stress falls, and no forms in the sheet carry stress marks. Position of word stress therefore remains undescribed.
new_statements.exceptions: None. (Notes mention two dialects differing in r/l and g/k, nothing prosodic.)
new_statements.domain_note: Orthography-oriented OPD sheet; statement is about phonemic status for writing purposes, not about phonetic stress placement; word vs phrase domain not addressed.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD covers the whole language (villages Asang, Reite, Serieng, Sorang; alternate name Nekeni/Nekene), i.e. nekg1240 itself, both dialects (Sorang-west and Reite-east per Claassen & McElhanon 1970). Note Glottolog classifies Nekgini as Finisterre-Huon > Gusap-Mot > Gira-Neko-Nekgini, not Rai Coast (Madang) despite its Rai Coast District location.
